title: Leading a team
summary: Assign the work, then handle what goes wrong.
intro: You have three people and one deadline. First you hand out the work. Then things start happening.

rows.label: The core feature — it can't slip

questions.prompt: Sarah gets sick for the week. How do you revise the plan?

options.label: Give it to James with daily check-ins
Give it to Mike and support him

questions.scenario: Sarah is unavailable. Review the assignments you made before deciding what needs covering.

variants.text: You assigned the core feature to Sarah. Her absence now leaves that deadline-critical work without its original owner.
You assigned the core feature to James. Sarah is unavailable, so consider her other assignments without automatically moving the core feature.
You assigned the core feature to Mike. Sarah is unavailable to help, so consider what support and coverage he needs.

questions.prompt: Mike makes a major mistake that costs the team a day.

options.label: Pair with him to fix it

variants.text: Your response to the absence was: Take it on myself. In this fictional continuation, Mike makes a mistake during a shared integration task; the team loses a day.
Your response to the absence was: Give it to James with daily check-ins. In this fictional continuation, Mike makes a mistake during a shared integration task; the team loses a day.
Your response to the absence was: Give it to Mike and support him. In this fictional continuation, Mike makes a mistake during a shared integration task; the team loses a day.
Your response to the absence was: Ask to move the deadline. In this fictional continuation, Mike makes a mistake during a shared integration task; the team loses a day.

questions.prompt: James has finished his current work early. How would you use the available time?

options.label: Let him pick what to do next

variants.text: After the integration mistake, you chose: Take the work back. James now has spare capacity. Reconsider who needs help in your revised plan.
After the integration mistake, you chose: Pair with him to fix it. James now has spare capacity. Reconsider who needs help in your revised plan.
After the integration mistake, you chose: Give him a formal warning. James now has spare capacity. Reconsider who needs help in your revised plan.
After the integration mistake, you chose: Let him fix it himself. James now has spare capacity. Reconsider who needs help in your revised plan.

questions.prompt: When stakes are high, how much do you trust newer people with important work?
Normally, how often do you give people work that stretches them?
Your only senior engineer leaves in three months. Nobody else knows the system.
questions.need: the team's future depended on growing newer people

options.label: Keep her on critical work until her last day
Pair a junior with her now, even if it slows things down
Plan to hire a contractor later

questions.prompt: You're shipping software for a medical device. A bug could hurt patients.

options.label: Give the risky code to the most experienced person
Give it to a junior with a code review
Give it to whoever is free
